notes: EXAMPLE, not a machine's real configuration. Realistic macOS profile: a browser with the declared tabs, a chat app idle, a terminal running several sessions of a coding-agent CLI, idle for the whole run. Copy this file to workloads/local-nominal-mac.json, replace every <placeholder> with the paths on your machine, then pass it with --workload. A group whose placeholders are left in place is reported as 'not configured' and matches nothing.

groups.name: browser
exe_contains: <path fragment of your browser install, e.g. /Google Chrome.app/>
<second fragment if the main process runs from a code-signature clone>
groups.notes: Tab count and contents cannot be verified from outside the browser: reported as declared. Descendants (extension native hosts) are attributed to the browser. Some browsers run their main process from a clone under /private/var/folders/..., which an /Applications prefix alone would miss.

groups.name: chat_app
exe_prefixes: <install prefix of your chat app, e.g. /Applications/Something.app/>

groups.name: coding_agent_cli
exe_contains: <path fragment of your agent CLI install>
groups.notes: A terminal coding-agent CLI. A session is a process of that CLI whose parent is not one. Such a CLI often has an executable named after its version while argv[0] is the CLI name, so both rules are useful.

groups.name: coding_agent_children
groups.notes: Every descendant of a session that is not itself the CLI (MCP servers, node, shells) is attributed to this group. The harness and what it starts are never included.

groups.name: coding_agent_orphans
cmdline_contains: <command-line fragment of the servers your agent CLI leaves behind, e.g. /.some-cli/plugins/>
groups.notes: Servers spawned by past sessions and left re-parented to launchd: they survive their session and keep consuming memory.
